applicability.rationale: A dashboard is a plausible intervention, but it does not by itself guarantee timely detection.

requestedIntervention.statement: Build a dashboard showing current production job status.
requestedIntervention.rationale: The dashboard was proposed as a means of reducing delayed detection.

desiredOutcomes.statement: Operators detect stalled production jobs within five minutes and can identify the responsible job without manually searching logs.
successMeasures: p95 stall-detection latency is at most five minutes
Manual log searches for initial detection fall materially

currentBaseline.description: Operators periodically inspect logs and also learn about stalled work from downstream complaints.
noChangeConsequences: Stalls may remain undetected for hours

causalHypothesis.statement: Event-driven alerts will reduce detection latency, while a small diagnostic view will accelerate triage after an alert.
causalHypothesis.mechanism: The system detects an age/state condition automatically, notifies the responsible operator, and links to current job context.
assumptions: Job state and age are reliable
An on-call or responsible operator can receive notifications
Alert thresholds can avoid unacceptable noise
falsifiers: The authoritative job state cannot distinguish healthy long-running work from a stall

constraints.statement: The solution must operate on the internal network and use the existing job-state source.
A browser-based diagnostic view is preferred.

risks: Stalls remain unnoticed when nobody is watching

alternatives.intervention: Event-driven alerting with a small diagnostic dashboard
costs: Alert rules and routing must be operated

alternatives.intervention: Automatically restart every apparently stalled job
risks: Duplicate effects or hidden root causes

counterfactual.question: If the dashboard were delivered exactly as requested, under what circumstances would delayed stall detection remain?
failureConditions: No operator is watching the dashboard
The display becomes stale without an obvious health signal
The job state cannot distinguish a stall
residualRisks: Threshold tuning may produce alert noise
Some stalls may require domain-specific detectors
counterfactual.conclusion: A passive dashboard is insufficient for the detection outcome; active alerting plus a diagnostic view is the better intervention.

successEvidence.measure: Time from qualifying stall condition to operator acknowledgement
successEvidence.thresholdOrSignal: p95 at most five minutes under the agreed operational scenario
successEvidence.observationWindow: initial operational assessment and first 30 days

successEvidence.measure: Manual log searches used for first detection
successEvidence.thresholdOrSignal: Material reduction from the documented baseline

risk.rationale: Delayed production detection has material operational consequences and the intervention crosses job-state, notification, and operator-workflow boundaries.

disposition.selectedDirection: Implement event-driven stall alerting with a small diagnostic dashboard and explicit alert-health observability.
disposition.rationale: This direction targets detection latency rather than assuming the operator will continuously watch a display.
investigationPlan: Prototype stall classification and alert-noise thresholds before full implementation

criteria: Requested intervention is treated as a candidate
Alternative and no-change directions were considered
Success evidence closes the causal claim
